title: Apuleius Writes The Golden Ass — Classical Witch Imagery
description: Apuleius of Madauros composed his novel Metamorphoses (known as The Golden Ass) around 150 CE, featuring the witch Pamphile who transforms herself into an owl and the protagonist Lucius who is accidentally turned into a donkey. The text provides the most detailed literary account of classical witch practice, including ointment application for shape-shifting, nocturnal flying, and the gathering of body parts from corpses. The witch Meroe in Book 1 also appears as a threatening figure who punishes her lovers with magical vengeance. This work directly influenced later medieval and early modern representations of the witch, particularly the flying witch with magical ointment.
historiographical_note: Stuart Clark and Hans Peter Broedel have both analyzed Apuleius as a direct literary source for the Malleus Maleficarum's accounts of witch ointments and shape-shifting, demonstrating direct textual transmission of classical witch imagery into early modern demonology.
source_method: Published scholarship; Apuleius Metamorphoses; secondary classical scholarship
